newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Sydney Olympic organisers lose another executive.
newsitem.headline: Sydney Olympic organisers lose another executive.

text.p: The finance director for the Sydney 2000 Olympic Games organising committee has resigned, bringing to three the number of senior executives to quit this year, an Olympic official said on Thursday.
The Sydney Organising Committee for the Olympic Games (SOCOG) has also seen two presidents quit this year.
Finance director John Pope's departure on Monday follows the resignation of the cultural director Jonah Jones in September and the communications director Lesley Russell in April.
The SOCOG spokesman described Pope's departure as "natural evolution", particularly after the committee examined organisational models used at the Atlanta Games this year.
"We are making structural changes following the Atlanta experience and are looking at a more strategic focus rather than just financial management," the spokesman told Reuters.
"It's an ever-changing organisation and probably the fastest-growing organisation in Australia," he said.
The SOCOG spokesman said Pope had left "to seek a senior finance position in the corporate sector".
The rash of executive departures has been mirrored in the SOCOG boardroom.
John Iliffe, chairman of major Australian retailer Woolworths and insurance firm GIO Australia, resigned in September after taking over as SOCOG president in March.
Iliffe replaced Gary Pemberton, the chairman of Qantas Airways. Pemberton was appointed SOCOG boss in 1994.
Pemberton stayed in the job during an eight-month search for a president after two candidates withdrew at the last moment.
Iliffe's departure saw the New South Wales state government's Olympics Minister Michael Knight become SOCOG president.

SOCOG began with a staff of 20 when Sydney won the right to host the 2000 Games in 1993. The spokesman said there was currently 150 staff at SOCOG and that number would grow to 1,500 by the time the Games began in September 2000.
